section.name: General
section.p: Please read the general Migration Guide page first, for common considerations that apply to migration or upgrade between versions of Apache Tomcat®.

section.name: Migrating from 11.0.x to 12.0.x
section.p: This section lists all the known changes between 11.0.x and 12.0.x which may cause backwards compatibility problems when upgrading.

subsection.name: Java 21 required
subsection.p: Apache Tomcat 12.0.x requires Java 21 or later. Apache Tomcat 11.0.x required Java 17.

subsection.name: Specification APIs
subsection.p: Apache Tomcat 12.0 supports the Jakarta Servlet 6.2, Jakarta Pages 4.1, Jakarta Expression Language 6.1, JakartaWebSocket 2.3, Jakarta Authentication 3.2 and Jakarta Annotations 3.1 specifications.

subsection.name: WebSocket 2.3
subsection.p: ClientEndpointConfig.Configurator.afterResponse() is now called after every WebSocket handshake regardless of whether the handshake is successful or not.
When attempting to write a message via a WebSocket session that has been closed, an IOException rather than an IllegalStateExcpetion is thrown for consistency with Writer and OutputStream.

subsection.name: Internal APIs
subsection.p: Whilst the Tomcat 12.0 internal API is broadly compatible with Tomcat 11.0 there have been many changes at the detail level and they are not binary compatible. Developers of custom components that interact with Tomcat's internals should review the JavaDoc for the relevant API.

ul.li: All code marked as deprecated in 11.0.x has been removed.
The useAcceptRanges initialisation parameter for the default servlet has been removed. It is now effectively hard coded to true
The default for the encodedSolidusHandling attribute of a Context has changed from decode to reject.
When searching the web application class loader for a resource or resources by name, align the behaviour with the JRE class loaders and always return null if the provided name starts with /.

The default value for the allowPostAsGet initialisation parameter of the Default servlet has been updated from true to false. This means a direct request (i.e. not a forward or an include) for a static resource using the POST method will be rejected by default.

Calls to HttpServletRequest.getContextPath() now return the canonical context path for the web application rather than the component of the request URI presented by the user agent that maps to the context path.
The default value of the archiveIndexStrategy attribute of the Resources element has been changed from simple to bloom to improve web application class loading performance.
The default for the digestInRfc3112Order attribute of MessageDigestCredentialHandler has been changed from false to true.
The default value of the cookiesWithoutEquals attribute of the Rfc6265CookieProcessor has been changed from name to ignore.
The default password value (was changeit) for the certificateKeystorePassword attribute of a certificate has been removed.
Support for HTTP/0.9 has been removed.

section.name: Upgrading 12.0.x
section.p: When upgrading instances of Apache Tomcat from one version of Tomcat 12.0 to another, particularly when using separate locations for $CATALINA_HOME and $CATALINA_BASE, it is necessary to ensure that any changes in the configuration files such as new attributes and changes to defaults are applied as part of the upgrade. To assist with the identification of these changes, the form below may be used to view the differences between the configuration files in different versions of Tomcat 12.0.

subsection.name: Tomcat 12.0.x noteable changes
subsection.p: The Tomcat developers aim for each stable patch release to be fully backwards compatible with the previous release. Occasionally, it is necessary to break backwards compatibility in order to fix a bug. In most cases, these changes will go unnoticed. This section lists changes that are not fully backwards compatible and might cause breakage when upgrading.

subsection.name: Tomcat 12.0.x configuration file differences
subsection.p: Select a configuration file, old version and new version from the boxes below and then click "View differences" to see the differences. The differences will be shown in a new tab/window.
Note: If there are no differences you will see an error page.
